thread.title_full: Experience overload this fall for Solon football - NewsBreak

author: Douglas Miles
title: Experience overload this fall for Solon football - NewsBreak
text:
By Douglas Miles ,
17 hours ago
SOLON — A football team can get far with ample experience.
After finishing last season one step shy of the state championship game, the Solon Spartans hope a bevy of returning players will be enough to take another step in 2026.
“The experience that we bring back, that makes us feel really good,” said seventh-year Solon Coach Lucas Stanton, who will lead the Spartans into their season-opening game Friday at Davenport Assumption. “With that experience, to build off of that would be seeing how guys go about their business. There is a little bit something bigger. You can tell they were working towards this year.”
Solon won its first 11 games last year before falling to Nevada in a Class 3A state semifinal at the UNI-Dome. For this year’s seniors, having a season end at the Dome twice in three years fueled an offseason of preparation.
“We have the same knitted culture in here,” Solon senior lineman Lucas Feuerbach said. “We are hungrier than last year, for sure. I feel a lot more excitement in practice, definitely. … I think most of us are really motivated. … Really excited to get another chance with the same guys. It just makes us hungrier.”
A South Dakota defensive tackle commit, the 6-foot-3, 260-pound Feuerbach will also anchor the Solon offensive line from the right tackle position, where he earned all-state honors as a freshman. Throw in last season’s all-state nod at defensive tackle, and Feuerbach is one of a whopping seven returning all-staters for Solon.
“A lot of returning guys,” senior Maddox Kelley said. “Coaching staff is great, players are great. Big things ahead. It will be good.”
While Kelley was an all-state receiver last year, he did everything for the Spartans. On offense, the 5-foot-10, 185-pound multisport athlete led the team with 50 receptions and 702 yards with 14 touchdowns while also rushing for 371 yards and 12 more scores. As a defensive back, Kelley registered 48 tackles and six interceptions and returned two for touchdowns.
This season, Kelley will add quarterback to his repertoire.
“Anything to help the team,” Kelley said. “After last season, I kind of had a guess that I would be at quarterback. Just somewhere where I can help the team the most. When they told me I was going to be making the switch there, the mentality is not, ‘Well, I get the ball more.’ It’s just, ‘How can I help the team as much as I can to win?’”
Kelley’s position switch hardly leaves the receiver room barren. Two more all-staters, seniors Kaden Hoeper (42 receptions, 691 yards, nine TDs) and Cody Milliman (35 receptions, 516 yards, four TDs) will provide enticing targets.
“We’ve got a ton of good athletes there,” Stanton said. “Multisport guys that aren’t just football. They’re basketball, they’re baseball, they’re track. We’re super-deep at that position.”
Feuerbach and all-state left guard Bradyn Schnoor will welcome a new left tackle in senior Simon Einwalter to the offensive line with the center and right guard positions up for grabs. Another competition is brewing at tailback, where senior track standout Jackson Burk is in the mix alongside junior speedsters Foster Owens and Sawyer Hancox.
“That’s an area for growth for us,” Stanton said. “Last year, running-wise our run game wasn’t where I would like it to be. Our strength was wide receiver and quarterback. We’re going to play to our strengths, but in Class 3A Iowa football, you are going to have to run the ball at some point.”
Last season, Solon’s defense yielded less than 10 points per game and this year’s bunch should be just as stingy. Solon’s defensive strength starts up front with Feuerbach (87 tackles, four sacks) and Schnoor at defensive tackle with Einwalter (14 tackles for loss) and all-stater James Thomsen (55 tackles, 5 1/2 sacks) at defensive ends.
“Those four, it is probably hard to find a better four,” Stanton said. “We’ve had some pretty good ones in my time, but that package of those four is as good as we have seen.”
At linebacker, a robust competition continues at camp between Owens, fellow junior Colin Dunn and seniors Luis Buck and Ian Kronk.
“It’s a really good group,” Stanton said. “It’s a really good group of guys that have just that tradition at linebacker that we have. They waited their turn and have been really coachable. I’d feel comfortable putting any two of that combination out there.”
Even with the added responsibility of quarterback, Kelley will man the secondary alongside Hoeper and fellow safety Paxton Holtcamp plus some combination of cornerbacks Michael Bigelow, Grant Gordon, Jonathan Thomson and Burk.
“It will be fun,” said Kelley, who holds a scholarship offer from Drake. “Just helping the team out as best as I can. Thought I was going to stay at rover, but they decided to move me. Whatever helps the team the best. Whatever you want me to do, I’ll do.”
Senior Collin McKie returns after an all-state season at punter and figures to be in line for placekicking duties, as well.
The non-district portion of the schedule will present early challenges. After the opener at Assumption, Solon hosts Williamsburg, travels to Mount Vernon for the annual Highway 1 clash before welcoming Benton Community to Spartan Stadium.
“The first four games are pretty tough,” Kelley said. “If we can get through those, I think that will really help. … Just playing to our standard every game. If we can do that, I think we can really beat teams.”
The 3A-4 district includes Fairfield, Fort Madison, Keokuk, Mount Pleasant and Washington.
“I think Mount Pleasant is going to be much improved,” Stanton said. “They’ll have some size and be improved athletically. I think Washington is a proud program. They have had a lot of success, they have just been down the last couple of years. Their numbers are up and I think they are going to be pretty salty. They’re going to be a challenge.”
